papers.title: Memory Efficient Reinforcement Learning for Microcontroller Class Edge Devices: Near DQN Control at a Fraction of the Memory in Solar-Powered Street Lighting
papers.summary: Solar-powered street lights and similar smart city nodes must decide, minute by minute, how much to sense, which on-device model to run, and how brightly to light, all from a small battery and a modest panel, on a microcontroller with very little memory. Reinforcement learning (RL) can learn this trade-off, but most reported controllers say little about what the policy itself costs to store. papers.title: KYNEMA: Design and Validation of Multi-Modal Robot Interaction for XR-Based Robotics Education
papers.summary: Hands-on interaction with robots is valuable for robotics education, but hardware access is limited by cost, laboratory capacity, and safety, and 2D interfaces poorly represent real workspaces. We developed a browser-native extended reality (XR) application that displays laboratory robots at true scale in the user's environment and offers three manipulation modes: direct joint control, forward-kinematics control, and inverse-kinematics teleoperation. papers.title: Model & Locomotion Dynamics of a Goat Bio-Inspired Quadruped Robot Through Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Traditional control methods struggle to handle high-degree-of-freedom systems and the unpredictability of real-world dynamics. Deep Reinforcement Learning has emerged to overcome this limitation, becoming central to autonomous robotic control and enabling greater agility and adaptability in legged robots. A custom 12-DOF goat-inspired quadruped was trained via PPO-based imitation learning against a reference trajectory built from real ovine motion-capture data. papers.title: AnyNav: Visual neuro-symbolic friction learning for off-road navigation
papers.summary: Off-road navigation is critical for a wide range of field robotics applications from planetary exploration to disaster response. However, it remains a longstanding challenge due to unstructured environments and the inherently complex terrain–vehicle interactions. Traditional physics-based methods struggle to accurately capture the nonlinear dynamics underlying these interactions, while purely data-driven approaches often overfit to specific motion patterns, vehicle geometries, or platforms, limiting their generalization in diverse, real-world scenarios. papers.title: INTERACTIVE MELODY GENERATION AND ROBOTIC SAXOPHONE PERFORMANCE: THE ROBOSAX MELODY SLOT MACHINE
papers.summary: This paper presents RoboSax Melody Slot Machine, a system that combines Melody Slot Machine, a dial-based interface for exploring melodically coherent variations, with RoboSax, a robotic saxophone that automates fingering with servo motors. Selected melodies are transmitted as MIDI to RoboSax, while the performer supplies breath and articulation. Because the melodic variations are generated by a GTTM-based morphing method, users can explore related phrases without losing structural coherence. The system therefore supports both accessible melody creation and embodied wind-instrument performance

papers.title: Design and Experimental Validation of an Underactuated Anthropomorphic Robotic Hand Based on the Ball-Ring-Elliptical Mechanism
papers.summary: This work reports the fabrication and experimental characterization of an underactuated anthropomorphic hand based on the Ball-Ring-Elliptical (BRE) rigid-soft finger of Zhang et al., originally validated on a single multi-material PolyJet prototype. The BRE equations were reconstructed in parametric CAD and printed at several scales on commodity printers, yielding four flexion-only fingers, each driven by one servomotor and one compliant tendon and characterized with single-camera tracking and servo-current sensing. papers.title: Vibration Reduction in a Single-Degree-of-Freedom Flexible Arm via Model Predictive Control and Deep Learning
papers.summary: Single-degree-of-freedom flexible robotic arms are an attractive alternative to rigid manipulators due to their lower mass and energy consumption and greater maneuverability, but their low structural stiffness produces residual vibrations that degrade positioning accuracy. This work presents the experimental implementation of a Model Predictive Controller (MPC) for a single-degree-of-freedom flexible arm, complemented by a Deep Q-Learning (DQN) supervisor that selects online among three weighting profiles of the MPC cost function. papers.title: RoboLab AR: An Augmented Reality Laboratory Environment for Progressive Robotics Education in Latin American Universities
papers.summary: This paper presents RoboLab AR, an open-source desktop robotics laboratory structured into five progressive hands-on practices: fundamental kinematics, custom CAD integration, obstacle-aware motion planning, multibody dynamic control, and physical mockup validation via augmented reality (AR). papers.title: A Methodological Proposal for Developing a Multi-Task Mobile Robot Adapted to Open-Field Agriculture
papers.summary: This paper presents a methodological proposal and a conceptual design framework for developing a multi-task mobile robotic platform tailored for open-field agriculture. Faced with rural demographic crises, population aging, and severe labor shortages in Latin America, open-field automation stands as a vital socio-economic and technological imperative that transcends the limits of traditional greenhouses. papers.summary: Atrial fibrillation (AF) poses significant clinical challenges due to the complex and variable geometry of the left atrial appendage (LAA), whose structure complicates the development of personalized interventions like LAA occlusion (LAAO) for stroke prevention Current reliance on animal models and cadavers for the assessment of left atrium (LA) and LAA to study AF-related disease and interventions raises reproducibility concerns, necessitating the development of high fidelity, physiologically relevant tools. papers.title: The influence of music on technical skill in robotic surgery among general surgery residents: a simulation-based experimental study
papers.summary: Music is commonly played in operating rooms, but its effect on the acquisition of robotic surgical skills is unclear, particularly when the music is chosen by the trainee. This study evaluated whether a personalized musical intervention influences the technical performance of general surgery residents on a robotic surgery simulator. papers.title: Towards a competence-behaviour-design alignment for educational robotics kits: a theoretical synthesis and development principles
papers.summary: Abstract Educational robotics kits (ERKs) are widely used to support competence-oriented technology education, yet their design is rarely grounded in clearly prioritised technological competences and associated learning behaviours. This research, situated in China’s General Technology curriculum, addresses this gap by developing a competence-behaviour-design (C-B-D) alignment for ERKs. papers.summary: The increasing deployment of autonomous robots in dynamic and uncertain environments has created substantial computational requirements associated with motion planning, collision detection, inverse kinematics, forward kinematics, dynamics estimation, trajectory optimization, and real-time control. papers.title: Design and Experimental Evaluation of a Low-Cost Autonomous Medical Rescue Robot for Hazardous and Conflict-Affected Environments
papers.summary: Emergency rescue operations in hazardous, unstable, and conflict-affected environments expose medical teams and first responders to serious risks, including structural collapse, fire, debris, toxic exposure, communication failure, and restricted access to victims. Robotic systems can reduce direct human exposure by performing early reconnaissance, detecting possible human presence, transmitting visual information, and supporting rescue planning. papers.title: WARMTH, COMPETENCE, OR BOTH? DUAL-PATHWAY CONCEPTUALISATION OF ROBOTIC RESTAURANT ENCOUNTER AND CUSTOMER REVISIT INTENTION
papers.summary: Service robots have become a routine presence in restaurants across Asia, yet customer responses to them remain ambivalent. Studies of service robots in hospitality typically bundle the attributes of the machine into a single quality score and regress satisfaction on it. Social cognition research suggests a different structure. papers.title: REAL-TIME DETECTION AND ANALYSIS OF VEHICLE SPEED BASED ON COMPUTER VISION TECHNOLOGIES
papers.summary: This paper proposes software for detecting and analyzing the speed of motor vehicles based on images obtained from video surveillance cameras. The system relies on computer vision methods: vehicles are detected using the YOLOv8 neural network, tracked across the frame sequence by the ByteTrack algorithm, and pixel coordinates are converted into real metric distances by means of a homography matrix. papers.title: Tunisian Licence Plate
papers.summary: This dataset was collected and developed as part of an applied artificial intelligence and computer vision project at Pixemantic, focusing on Automatic License Plate Recognition (ALPR) and intelligent transportation systems. papers.title: A Comparative Study of Computer Vision-Based Attendance Recognition Systems
papers.summary: Manual attendance management is time-consuming, error-prone and open to proxy attendance. This work studies automated computer vision based student attendance and classroom engagement monitoring systems for real-time classroom environments. It reviews seventeen recent papers (2025–2026) and builds on a base paper that uses multi-face recognition with FaceNet-based 128-dimensional embeddings.
